FOREWORD

This Indian Standard (Part 5) (First Revision) which is identical with ISO 1442:1997 `Meat and meat products -- Determination of moisture content (Reference method)' issued by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on the recommendation of the Slaughter House and Meat Industry Sectional Committee and approval of the Food and Agriculture Division Council. This standard was originally under dual numbering. published in 1971. It is being revised to harmonize with ISO 1442:1997

Indian Standard
MEAT AND MEAT PRODUCTS -- METHODS OF TEST
PART 5 DETERMINATION OF MOISTURE CONTENT (REFERENCE METHOD)

(First Revision )
1 Scope This International Standard specifies a reference method for the determination of the moisture content of meat and
meat products.

2 Definitions
For the purposes of this International Standard, the following definitions apply. 2.1 moisture content of meat and meat products: Loss in mass obtained
specified in this.lnternational Standard, divided by the mass of the test portion. by mass. obtained by carrying out a specified test method. [ISO 5725-1] under the operating conditions

Moisture content is expressed as a percentage 2.2

test result: The value of a characteristic

3 Principle
Thorough mixing of the test portion with sand and drying to constant mass at 103 "C b 2 "C.

4 Material
4.1 Sand, clean, acid-washed, of a size such that it passes through a sieve of aperture size 1,4 mm and stays on a
sieve of aperture size 250 Am. Dry the sand before use at 150 "C to 160 `C and store in an airtight closed bottle.
NOTE -- If clean (acid-washed) sand is not available, the sand maybe cleaned by the following procedure,

Wash the sand with running water. Boil the sand with dilute hydrochloric

acid, no = 1,19 g/ml, diluted (1 + 1), for 30 min while stirring continuously. Repeat the boiling operation with another portion of the acid until the acid no longer turns yellow after boiling. Wash the sand with distilled water until the test for chloride is negative, For storage, dry the sand at 150 "C to 160 `C.

5 Apparatus
Usual laboratory apparatus and, in particular, the following.

5.1 Mechanical or electrical equipment capable of homogenizing the laboratory sample. This includes a highspeed rotational cutter, or a mincer fitted with a plate with holes not exceeding 4,0 mm in diameter.
5.2 Flat dish, made of porcelain or metal (e.g. nickel, aluminium, height about 25 mm, stainless steel), of diameter at least 60 mm and

5.3 Thin glass rod, flattened at one end, slightly longer than the diameter of the dish (5.2). 5.4 Drying oven, electrically heated, capable of operating at 103 "C ~ 2 "C.

5.5 Desiccator, containing an efficient desiccant, such as silica gel.
5.6 Analytical balance, capable of weighing to the nearest 0,001 g.

6 Sampling
It is important that the laboratory receive a sample which is truly representative changed during transport or storage.
Sampling is not part of the method specified in this International given in ISO 3100-1. Proceed from a representative sample of at least 200 g. and change in composition are prevented. and has not been damaged or

Standard. A recommended

sampling

method is

Store the sample in such a way that deterioration

7" Preparation

of test sample

Homogenize the laboratory sample with the appropriate equipment (5.1 ). Take care that the temperature of the sample material does not rise above 25 "C. If a mincer is used, pass the sample at least twice through the equipment. Fill a suitable airtight container with the prepared test sample, close the container and store in such a way that deterioration and change in composition are prevented. Analyse the test sample as soon as practicable, but always within 24 h after homogenization.

8 Procedure
NOTE -- If it is required to check whether the repeatability accordance with 8.3 under repeatability conditions. limit (10,2) is met, carry out two single determinations in

8.1

Preparation

of the dish and sand

Transfer to the dish (5.2) a quantity of sand (4.1) equal to three to four times the mass of the test portion (see 8.2) and dry the dish, sand and glass rod (5.3) for 30 min in the oven (5.4) set at 103 "C. Allow the dish with its contents and the glass rod to cool in the desiccator (5.5) to room temperature the nearest 0,001 g (mo). 8.2 and weigh to

Test portion
the dish

Transfer between 5 g to 8 g of the prepared test sample (clause 7) to the prepared dish (8.1) and weigh with its contents and the glass rod to the nearest 0,001 g (ml). 8.3

Determination

8.3.1 Mix the contents of the dish by means of the glass rod (5.3).
NOTE -- In cases of difficulty in mixing the test portion with sand, ethanol ethanol should be evaporated gently before drying the sample in the oven.
may be added as necessaty. In this case, the

Heat the dish with its contents and the glass rod for 2 h in the oven (5.4) set at 103 "C. Remove the dish with its contents and the glass rod from the oven and place them in the desiccator (5.5). Allow the dish, its contents and the glass rod to cool to room temperature, 8.3.2 then weigh to the nearest 0,001 g.

weighings

Repeat the heating, cooling and weighing operations specified in 8.3.1 until the results of two successive (m2), separated by 1 h of heating, do not differ by more than O,'1 YO of the mass of the test potilon.

9 Expression of results
Calculate the moisture content, w, as a percentage by mass, using the following equation:

is the mass, in grams, of the dish, rod and sand (8.1"); is the mass, in grams, of the dish containing the test portion, rod and sand, before drying (8.2); is the mass, in grams, of the dish containing the test portion, rod and sand, after drying (8.3.2).

Report the result rounded to one decimal place.

10 Precision
10.1 Interlaboratory test

Details of an interlaboratory test on the precision of the method are given in ref. [3]. The values derived from this interlaboratory test may not be applicable to concentration ranges and matrices other than those given.

10.2 Repeatability
The absolute difference between two independent single test results, obtained using the same method on identical test material in the same laboratory by the same operator using the same equipment within a short interval of time, should not be greater than the value of r given by the formula r=0,593Y0 +0,0017 W

where x is the mean moisture content of both results, expressed as a percentage by mass.

10.3 Reproducibility
The absolute difference between two single test results obtained using the same method on identical test material in different laboratories with different operators using different equipment, should not be greater than the value of R given by the formula. R=0,797
yO

+0,004 71%

where z is the mean moisture content of both results, expressed as a percentage by mass.

11 Test report
The test report shall specify -- the method in accordance -- the method used; -- the test result(s) obtained; and -- if the repeatability has been checked, the final quoted result obtained. Standard, or regarded as optional, with which sampling was carried out (if known);

It shall also mention all operating details not specified in this International together with details of any incidents which may have influenced the result. The test report shall include all information

necessary for the complete identification

of the sample.
